column3: The Hebrew actively says Hanun reigned in his father’s place; BSB describes the father as being succeeded.
The Hebrew repeats David’s name when he sends and explicitly calls the arriving group David’s servants; BSB uses pronouns and adds “some.”
The Hebrew retains the eyes image in the first question; BSB uses “do you really believe.”
The Hebrew explicitly says the garments were cut in half and names the buttocks as the endpoint; BSB has “at the hips.”
The Hebrew actively says unnamed people reported this; BSB uses passive “was reported.” The beard is singular in Hebrew and plural in BSB.
The Hebrew repeats the Ammonites as those sending, and names the king of Maacah directly; BSB specifies men from that king.
The Hebrew does not explicitly call the gate a city gate.
The Hebrew uses the singular face of the battle; BSB uses plural “battle lines.”
The Hebrew calls the remaining group “the people” and retains the hand image; BSB uses “forces” and “under the command.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and does not explicitly say the helper will come in the first condition; BSB supplies Joab and “come.”
The Hebrew repeats the strength root; BSB makes fighting explicit in its second expression.
The Hebrew calls those with Joab “the people”; BSB says “troops.”
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat fighting in the description of Joab’s return.
The Hebrew says they assembled together; BSB expresses this as regrouping.
The Hebrew names only “the river,” without Euphrates or “more” Arameans.
The Hebrew has forty thousand horsemen; BSB has foot soldiers. It names seven hundred chariots metonymically, where BSB specifies charioteers.
The Hebrew calls these kings Hadadezer’s servants and says they served Israel; BSB uses being subject in both cases.
